map.已知总体方差时的单样本 Z 检验: One-sample Z test with known population variance
map.支持双侧、左尾、右尾三种备择假设: Supports three alternative hypotheses: two-sided, left-tailed and right-tailed
map.给出 Z 统计量、p 值与结论: Gives the Z statistic, the p value and the conclusion
map.用于判断改版前后差异是否显著: Used to judge whether the difference before and after a redesign is significant
map.已知总体方差时检验样本均值是否等于假设值。: Test whether the sample mean equals the hypothesized value when the population variance is known.
map.判断改版是否真的有效：把改版前后的数据代入检验，看 p 值是否小于显著性水平，而: Judge whether a redesign really worked: put the before and after data into the test and check whether the p value is below the significance level, rather than just looking at whether the numbers differ.
map.填假设的总体均值 μ₀（改版前的基准值）: Enter the hypothesized population mean mu0 (the baseline value before the redesign)
map.填总体标准差 σ（必须是已知的总体值，不是样本标准差）: Enter the population standard deviation sigma (it must be the known population value, not the sample standard deviation)
map.填样本均值与样本量 n: Enter the sample mean and the sample size n
map.选择检验方向：双侧看是否有差异，单侧看是否变大或变小: Choose the test direction: two-sided checks whether there is any difference, one-sided checks whether it became larger or smaller
map.看 p 值：小于显著性水平（如 0.05）才拒绝原假设，别只看均值数值有变化: Look at the p value: reject the null hypothesis only when it is below the significance level (such as 0.05); do not decide just because the mean changed numerically
map.样本量很大时，微小到没有业务价值的差异也会显著；因此应同时看效应量与置信区间，并: With a very large sample, differences too small to have business value also become significant; so look at the effect size and the confidence interval as well, and fix the decision rule before the experiment
map.已知 σ 用 Z；σ 未知用样本 s 且小样本用 t。: When sigma is known use Z; when sigma is unknown use the sample s and, for small samples, t.
map.p 值小于 0.05 就说明有效吗？: Does a p value below 0.05 mean it is effective?
map.只能说「在总体无差异的假设下，观察到这么极端结果的概率不足 5%」。它不等于「有: You can only say that "under the assumption of no difference in the population, the probability of observing a result this extreme is under 5%". It does not mean "there is a 95% probability that it works", nor that the effect is large enough. With a very large sample, differences too small to have business value also become significant; so look at the effect size and the confidence interval as well, and fix the decision rule before running the experiment.
